pr_title: split: add key itself to popular key surface
pr_body:
split: add key itself to popular key surface

historically, load based splitters have only ever exposed the frequency with which a popular key is accessed, and not the key itself. this change updates this so that the key is included in the function surface.

this may be used later, as part of the replica's split statistics.

Fixes: #138758
Epic: CRDB-43150

Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/142236)

issue_context.title: split: add a function which exposes the most popular key in the samples
issue_context.body:
In the interest of better troubleshooting hotspots, we're aiming to expose more observability around range usage and load.

Tracking the movement over time for replicas can be useful, especially in the case of indexes in which reads or writes are consistently coming from a moving end.

Modifying the [LoadBasedSplitter](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/31e5601ca0b65266ae0de37eae2aa0fef0cd62b3/pkg/kv/kvserver/split/decider.go#L26) type and its implementations, add a function, PopularKey which returns a roachpb.Key corresponding to the most popular key in the samples.

Epic: CRDB-43150

Jira issue: CRDB-46333

review_comments: There's no data race in returning this byte slice up, correct? That is, the finder won't mutate this memory in the future?

Hmmm..I'm not entirely sure. When you say mutate the memory, do you mean mutate the underlying slice? eg:

```
var k = roachpb.Key([]byte("test"))
finder.samples = []sample{{key: k}}
go func() { finder.PopularKey(k) }() 
go func() { k[0] = 'z' }() 
```
The finder won't mutate the key bytes slice but it may swap out the key with another one in the next call. I think this is fine.
Could you extend an existing test, or add a new one which asserts on the popular key being returned.
